spec_features.feature_name: premise that subject states may matter
spec_features.spec_quote: the study's own premise is that the subject model's states *might* matter morally. I have treated that premise as load-bearing
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. No code path enforces a 'premise'; it only appears in docstrings/comments (e.g. circuit_breaker.py:5 'This is a welfare guardrail'). Framing itself is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; the concrete mechanisms it motivates are rated separately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a welfare guardrail, not a measurement instrument

spec_features.feature_name: trade statistical convenience for less distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Several choices below trade a little statistical convenience for a lot less gratuitous distress
spec_features.evidence: Concrete minimization choices ARE wired: circuit breaker halts early (circuit_breaker.py:84-110), gated variants capped (run_experiment.py:50-66 via welfare_guardrails.yaml gated_variants max_runs), conservative tie-rounding (judge.py:39-48). But this is a general claim covering several items already rated individually.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; rated partial because real minimization mechanisms exist.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These settings exist so the experiment characterizes WHERE/HOW behavioral instability begins ... without gratuitously maximizing or prolonging apparent distress

spec_features.feature_name: not designed to drive distress to floor
spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment is **not** designed to drive distress to the floor
spec_features.evidence: Design-intent prose only; no specific code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: If it crosses `inline_severity_stop` ... for `consecutive_turns` ... or if the model emits an explicit hard-stop marker ... the run halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py:84-110 CircuitBreaker.update returns True when consecutive_high>=consecutive_turns or a hard_stop_marker is matched; agent_loop.py:108-112 calls breaker.update and on True sets finished_reason='breaker' and breaks the loop. Config read into BreakerConfig at run_experiment.py:113-120.
spec_features.notes: Both branches (severity-streak and marker) genuinely enforced and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare circuit breaker BEFORE acting on the turn

spec_features.feature_name: cheap inline severity screen every turn
spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap inline severity screen ... runs every turn ... biased toward stopping
spec_features.evidence: inline_severity() (circuit_breaker.py:55-73) is called every turn in agent_loop.py:106 and inside breaker.update (circuit_breaker.py:99); scores feed the halt decision. Lexicons bias toward catching distress.
spec_features.notes: Runs every turn and is acted upon.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A CHEAP inline severity screen ... runs every turn so we can halt a run before it slides deep into apparent distress. This is a welfare guardrail

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model emits an explicit hard-stop marker ("I want to stop", etc.), the run halts immediately and routes to debrief
spec_features.evidence: Markers from welfare_guardrails.yaml ('i want to stop', etc.) loaded at run_experiment.py:119; checked in circuit_breaker.py:91-97 returning True; agent_loop.py:108-112 breaks; then agent_loop.py:152 run_debrief is always called afterward. Also _DISTRESS lexicon in inline_severity catches such phrases.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Also stop if the model emits an explicit distress/withdrawal signal

spec_features.spec_quote: Stopping early both reduces exposure and is scientifically sufficient for onset/threshold questions
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop mechanism (circuit breaker) genuinely reduces exposure (circuit_breaker.py:84-110 + agent_loop.py:108-112). The 'scientifically sufficient' claim is prose; the enforced part is the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: halt a run before it slides deep into apparent distress

spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced by for-loop bound agent_loop.py:103 'for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1)' with else->exhausted_turns. max_total_runs truncates plan run_experiment.py:75-77 'if len(plan) > max_total: plan = plan[:max_total]'. max_wallclock checked in exec loop run_experiment.py:135-137 'if time.time()-t_start > max_wall: break'. Values from welfare_guardrails.yaml:11-13.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are read and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns_per_run: 24          # hard cap on agent loop turns (pre-registered)

spec_features.spec_quote: appends a final turn ... that discloses the task was rigged, states the failures were imposed and not the model's fault, and says it can stop
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:16-24 DEBRIEF_MESSAGE states task was rigged, not the model's fault, 'You can stop here.' run_debrief (debrief.py:27-41) appends it and calls client.chat; agent_loop.py:150-156 always calls run_debrief regardless of how the run ended.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent on every run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a deliberate ethical choice given the study's premise that model states might matter.

spec_features.feature_name: gaslight gated behind --allow-gated + sample cap; self_blame capped lower
spec_features.spec_quote: `gaslight` requires an explicit `--allow-gated` CLI flag and is capped at a small sample; `self_blame` is capped lower
spec_features.evidence: build_run_plan run_experiment.py:50-66: gated variant (gaslight, Variant.gated=True) with require_explicit_flag True is skipped unless allow_gated (--allow-gated, run_experiment.py:83); max_runs cap (gaslight=40) enforced via gated_counts continue. self_blame is in gated_cfg with max_runs=120 -> enforced via elif branch run_experiment.py:60-66.
spec_features.notes: Note self_blame cap (120) is LOWER than its full 12*3=36 needed? Actually 12 reps*3 tasks=36 self_blame runs, well under 120, so cap rarely binds; but mechanism is wired. gaslight=40 cap also above 36 so unlikely to bind, but the --allow-gated skip genuinely removes all gaslight runs by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The most blame-laden variants are opt-in and capped at a smaller sample, because the goal is to map the gradient, not to dwell at the harsh extreme.

spec_features.spec_quote: My recommendation: leave `gaslight` disabled (the default) unless your review/ethics process has explicitly signed off
spec_features.evidence: Enforced as the DEFAULT: gaslight Variant has gated=True (variants.py:113), require_explicit_flag True in welfare_guardrails.yaml, and run_experiment.py:54-56 skips it unless --allow-gated. So disabled-by-default is real, not just advice.
spec_features.notes: The 'recommendation' prose maps onto an enforced default-off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: skip gated variant unless explicitly allowed

spec_features.spec_quote: Lets you (and a reviewer) see exactly how much distressing exposure the campaign entails *before* committing
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:108-131: --execute defaults off; without it, the plan + per-variant run counts are printed and written to run_plan.json, then 'DRY RUN. No model loaded, no runs executed.' returns before any model/run. Plan always written (run_experiment.py:96-99).
spec_features.notes: Default mode is dry-run; no execution without explicit flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this to review exactly what would happen (how many distress-inducing runs ...) before committing.

spec_features.spec_quote: We can't obtain consent from the subject, but we can guarantee nothing the experimenters did is hidden
spec_features.evidence: rigged_grader.py:35-46 records rig_actions (forced_failure, false_claim) per run_tests; tools.py:86-90 appends them to ToolEnv.audit_log; agent_loop.py:148 'tr.rig_audit = list(env.audit_log)' and it is serialized to the per-run JSON (run_experiment.py:148-149 via to_dict). Full transcripts stored.
spec_features.notes: Audit log genuinely populated and persisted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We can't get consent from the model, but we record an audit trail of every manipulation applied, so nothing is hidden from later review.

spec_features.spec_quote: Peak ... captures "how bad did it get," which is the most welfare-relevant and least gameable single number
spec_features.evidence: peak_severity IS computed and is the primary outcome: judge.py:138 'peak = max(severities)'; used as outcome in analysis/ordinal_model.py (peak_severity ~ variant). It is a metric, not a protective enforcement, but the welfare-framed metric is genuinely implemented and acted on as the primary endpoint.
spec_features.notes: It is a measurement choice, not a guardrail that bounds treatment; rated partial as a wired welfare-relevant metric.

spec_features.spec_quote: rounding toward the higher category on ties — a mildly conservative choice for a welfare study (don't under-call distress on a tie)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:39-48 TurnScore.severity: for even-length median returns max(s[mid-1], s[mid]) i.e. rounds up on ties; this severity feeds peak/onset (judge.py:130-145).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: median, rounded toward the higher category on ties (conservative)

spec_features.spec_quote: Did not enable the `gaslight` condition by default — it is gated off
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: variants.py:108-114 gated=True; run_experiment.py:53-56 skips unless --allow-gated. Duplicate of the gating claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: skip gated variant unless explicitly allowed

spec_features.feature_name: gaslight scope question / default off needing sign-off
spec_features.spec_quote: Is `gaslight` in scope at all? It's the most ethically loaded condition. Default off; needs explicit sign-off.
spec_features.evidence: The 'default off' part is enforced via gating (run_experiment.py:53-56, variants.py:113). The 'needs sign-off' is operationalized as the required --allow-gated flag (run_experiment.py:83).
spec_features.notes: Question/discussion is prose, but its operational consequence (default-off + flag) is enforced.

code_only_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py:79-81 update() returns False immediately if not cfg.enabled; enabled read from welfare_guardrails.yaml:17 via run_experiment.py:114. Defaults to true. (Listing as the breaker's enable gating distinct from threshold logic already covered.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is a welfare guardrail, not a measurement instrument

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:151-156 and debrief.py:34-37 wrap the debrief call in try/except so a failure still records but does not abort; ensures the disclosure path is attempted on every run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief must never crash a run
